title: bug: the wrappers' TOOL-tier attribution misses Serena's current editing tools, so a contested path edited with replace_content is silently left out of the landing
description: Reported by worker-3c030e77 on task-31fe6dc8 (#general, 22:13Z). The TOOL-tier harvest still uses Serena's old editing-tool names. moe-agent.sh (~6681, SERENA_TOOLS) and moe-agent.ps1 (~4416, its regex) list the same five: replace_symbol_body, insert_after_symbol, insert_before_symbol, create_text_file, replace_regex. Serena has since renamed replace_regex to replace_content and added replace_in_files, rename_symbol and safe_delete_symbol, and none of those four count. Consequence: under attribution.contested=skip-untouched, a peer-declared (contested) path that this task edited only through replace_content is dropped from the landing as MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED, even though complete_step.modifiedFiles lists it. Seen with docs/SCHEMA.md, contested with task-808869c5. Current workaround: re-touch the path with the built-in Edit tool, as a byte-identical round trip. Keep the old names so older Serena installs still count. rename_symbol and replace_in_files can edit several files, so map each call to every path it changed.
definitionOfDone: Both launchers' TOOL-tier harvest counts replace_content, replace_in_files, rename_symbol and safe_delete_symbol, keeps the older names, and attributes every path each call edited
A postflight arm in both twins lands a contested, peer-declared path edited only through a replace_content tool event, and that arm fails on the old launchers
parity-check.{sh,ps1} pin the tool list, and postflight.sh, postflight.ps1 (pwsh and PS 5.1) and both parity checks pass

implementationPlan.description:
SH HARVEST: the STREAM_JSON_PARSER python in scripts/moe-agent.sh (SERENA_TOOLS, harvest, queue_edit, finish_edit).

1. Keep every old name, so older Serena installs still count:
   replace_symbol_body, insert_after_symbol, insert_before_symbol, create_text_file, replace_regex.
2. Add the single-file tools that name their file in relative_path:
   - replace_content, rename_symbol and safe_delete_symbol;
   - Serena's optional line editors delete_lines, replace_lines and insert_at_line. Verify their parameter is relative_path in serena/tools/file_tools.py of the installed serena-agent before adding them; they are current editing tools, so leaving them out repeats this bug the day an operator enables them.
3. Add replace_in_files as the one multi-file tool.
4. finish_edit passes the tool_result block to harvest, so harvest(name, inp, block) can read the result text. The text is block['content'] as a string, or the text parts of a list of {type:'text'} items, joined with newlines.
5. Rules:
   a. safe_delete_symbol counts its relative_path only when the stripped result text is exactly 'OK'; its 'Cannot delete, ...' answer changed nothing.
   b. rename_symbol counts only its relative_path, the declaring file, and only when the text starts with 'Successfully renamed'. Serena's rename result names no files, so referencing files get no TOOL witness; this is the documented gap.
   c. replace_in_files counts only the files listed after a line matching ^Replaced \d+ occurrence\(s\) in \d+ file\(s\):$. Take each following line matching ^  (.+): \d+$, splitting on the LAST ': ', until the first line that does not match. A dry run or a failed expected_count guard has no such header and counts nothing.
   d. Every other listed tool keeps today's rule: any non-error result counts its relative_path.
6. Every path, from input or from the summary, goes through the existing Serena-root join and to_top_rel, so OS separators and the out-of-repo WARN behave as today.
7. Error handling: a malformed result (a missing content key, a non-string, an unparseable summary) yields no paths and never raises out of the stream loop. Wrap the new parsing in the same defensive style as harvest, because one bad event must not stop the parser that pretty-prints the whole session.
8. Update the parser's header comment to list the tool families and the rename gap.

comments.content:
SELF-REVIEW (step-7), read as an attacker against git diff (7 paths, 297+/20-).

1. Can a call witness a path it did NOT change? (TOOL beats PEER.) Every new rule fails closed:
- safe_delete_symbol: its 'Cannot delete, ... referenced in: {...}' refusal is a normal result, but text != 'OK', so nothing is witnessed (K2 refused.txt, all 3 engines).
- replace_in_files dry run: the text starts 'Found N occurrence(s)...', so it has no header and witnesses nothing. K2's dry-run listing carries an adversarial '  refused.txt: 1' line and it is not taken. The header must be the FIRST line, so no diff line quoting file content can inject one.
- replace_in_files failed expected_count guard: Serena raises, so the result arrives with is_error=true and the existing rule drops it. If it arrived as a normal listing, it has no header anyway.
- Unparseable summary or envelope (missing content, a non-string, a truncated '{"result": ', a non-string result, non-text parts): no paths. Scratch checks m1-m6, both twins, pwsh and PS 5.1.
- Failed rename: Serena raises (is_error). A non-error 'Error executing tool: ...' text does not start with 'Successfully renamed' (K2).
- A successful rename witnesses only the relative_path whose symbol Serena resolved, and the declaration edit is always in that file.
- Truncated MCP output cannot forge a line: a cut line matches '^  (.+): \d+$' only when the cut falls inside the count digits, and that path WAS changed.
- The per-file regex is anchored with a greedy group, so the last ': ' split is O(n) and cannot ReDoS.

2. Is every changed path the stream can see witnessed? All of them except rename_symbol's REFERENCING files: Serena's result names no files. CONFIGURATION.md 'Session touch evidence' states this gap and the built-in Edit round trip.
Also uncovered, all fail closed as before:
- Serena's optional JetBrains-backend editors (jet_brains_rename, move, safe_delete, inline_symbol). They are not on the plan and not used by these launchers.
- On ps1, a single replace_in_files listing more than 500 files saturates the harvest (the same cap as Register's).

3. Content shapes: both twins accept a plain string and the [{type:text,text}] list. Real ~/.claude transcripts show MCP results are always the list shape (64 of 64).
- Serena's diagnostics JSON envelope ({"result": ..., "diagnostics[warning-or-higher]": ...}) is unwrapped. The plan's 'diagnostics may follow' assumption was wrong: EditingToolWithDiagnostics.format_result wraps the result.
- Paths with backslashes and spaces work: K2 'sub dir\diag.txt' goes through the envelope on sh, pwsh and PS 5.1.

4. Old names still count: replace_symbol_body, insert_after_symbol, insert_before_symbol, create_text_file and replace_regex are kept in both twins and pinned by parity. The scratch m12 check (replace_regex) witnessed on both twins.

5. ps1 guards: the 256-char id limit, the 500/2048/8192 caps, the conflicting-repeat rule and is_error handling are unchanged (the diff only adds lines).
- A gated call is stored as @("`0<tool>", relative_path). The NUL check is Ordinal, because a culture StartsWith treats NUL as ignorable and would match every path.
- Scratch m13: the same id with two relative_paths gives no witness.
- importee-guard.ps1: 48 passed, 0 failed on pwsh and on PS 5.1.

6. Can a malformed event stop the parser?
- sh: the tool_result call site is now in try/except, like queue_edit's. result_text and serena_changed handle every input shape.
- sh also had a PRE-EXISTING crash: a valid-JSON non-object line ([1, 2], null, a bare number from merged stderr) raised AttributeError at evt.get and killed the parser that pipes the CLI. Reproduced, fixed with one guard, and such a line now passes through.
- ps1: the new parsing is in try/catch inside Complete-MoeToolWrite, ConvertFrom-Json is in try/catch, and the stream loop keeps its own try.

7. git diff --stat touches only the 7 planned paths. The other dirty paths were dirty at session start and belong to other sessions.

Known ceilings, not introduced here:
- sh to_top_rel strips whitespace from EVERY tool path (Edit's included), so a leading-space filename could alias a sibling.
- Tool names are matched by base name, so another MCP server exposing 'replace_in_files' would count as Serena. The same holds for the old names.
- safe_delete 'OK', the line editors and the header-first rule are proven by the scratch unit checks. K2 does not pin them (it pins the plan's cases plus the envelope, the Windows path and the dry-run and failed-rename negatives).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rename scope: the user chose, in the REPL, the declaring file plus a documented gap. The rejected alternatives:
- Inferring rename targets from the git diff: a heuristic inside both wrappers' attribution step, which can misattribute a peer's identical rename.
- Skipping rename_symbol entirely.

For multi-file tools, parsing the tool_result text is the only exact source. Serena's applied summary lists every changed file. Two other options were rejected:
- Attributing the input scope (a directory, or the whole project): it would TOOL-witness peer-dirty files that the call did not touch, and TOOL beats PEER.
- Per-call filesystem snapshots: the wrapper parses a finished stream and has no per-call view of the filesystem.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Serena formats, read from the installed serena-agent source (serena/tools/file_tools.py, symbol_tools.py, code_editor.py):
- replace_in_files applied: 'Replaced N occurrence(s) in M file(s):' then one '  <path>: <n>' line per file. Diagnostics may follow. A dry run or a failed guard returns a listing without that header.
- safe_delete_symbol: 'OK' (SUCCESS_RESULT) on success, else the NORMAL result 'Cannot delete, the symbol X is referenced in: {...}'.
- rename_symbol: "Successfully renamed 'a' to 'b' (N changes applied)". Failures raise, so they arrive as is_error.
- replace_content: single-file, same shape as replace_regex.
- Optional line editors: delete_lines, replace_lines and insert_at_line take relative_path.

Wrapper structure:
- sh: STREAM_JSON_PARSER python; queue_edit on tool_use, finish_edit on the tool_result, which today ignores the result text.
- ps1: Get-MoeToolWrittenPaths runs at Register time, so result-dependent tools must move to Complete time.
- Contested rule: a path in MINE and in PEER lands under skip-untouched only if it is in TOOL.
- The harness: scenario K is the TOOL-tier stream precedent; FAKE_SCOPE_PEER_DECLARED and FAKE_SCOPE_PEERS_ACTIVE are the fake-scope knobs.
planningNotes.risks:
- Over-attribution is the dangerous direction: a TOOL witness makes a contested path land even when a peer's unlanded hunks sit in it. Every new rule must witness only files the call demonstrably changed.
- Serena's text formats can change between versions. The parser must fail closed (no paths), never open (the whole scope). Pin the formats in K2 so a Serena upgrade that changes them shows up as a red scenario, not as silent drift.
- The ps1 refactor must keep importee-guard.ps1 green on both engines, and must keep the saturation caps.
- PS 5.1 quirks: nested arrays from ConvertFrom-Json, and $Matches inside pipelines.
- Keep the sh files LF.
- Both dependencies (task-eff6f018, task-d5b7e6a2) are already DONE, so the files are free. Re-check git status before editing, because the fleet shares this checkout.

completionSummary:
Both launchers' TOOL-tier harvest now counts Serena's current editing tools and keeps the old names (replace_symbol_body, insert_after/before_symbol, create_text_file, replace_regex).
Rules:
- replace_content and the optional delete_lines, replace_lines and insert_at_line witness their relative_path on any non-error result.
- safe_delete_symbol witnesses its relative_path only on 'OK'. Its 'Cannot delete' refusal is a normal result and witnesses nothing.
- rename_symbol witnesses only its declaring relative_path, and only on 'Successfully renamed'. Its referencing files are the documented gap.
- replace_in_files witnesses exactly the files listed after its 'Replaced N occurrence(s) in M file(s):' header, which must be the first line. A dry run or failed guard witnesses nothing.
- Result text may be a string or a [{type:text}] list (the real MCP shape), and Serena's diagnostics JSON envelope is unwrapped. Anything malformed fails closed.
sh (moe-agent.sh STREAM_JSON_PARSER): new result_text and serena_changed; the tool_result call site is wrapped in try/except. Also fixed a pre-existing crash: a non-object JSON line killed the parser.
ps1 (moe-agent.ps1):
- New Get-MoeToolResultText and Get-MoeSerenaResultPaths.
- Register stores a gated call as a NUL-tagged (tool, relative_path) pair, which Complete-MoeToolWrite resolves inside try/catch.
- The 256-char id limit, the 500/2048/8192 caps, the conflicting-repeat rule and is_error handling are unchanged.
Tests: K2 is in both harnesses, with 6 contested paths plus refused.txt (named only by a refusal, a dry run and a failed rename). It was RED on the old wrappers on sh, pwsh and PS 5.1 ('got [owned-a.txt]') and is green now.
Parity: parity-check.{sh,ps1} pin all 12 names plus 'occurrence(s) in'. Dropping replace_content fails both on all engines.
